speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how much feedback has LTA received from residents in the past year from speeding vehicles with modified engines; (b) what is the estimated time frame for LTA to conduct an investigation and to implement measures to address the issue; and (c) whether the Traffic Police cameras that are located in the area will be equipped to capture the footage related to this problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA conducts onsite checks on the reported vehicles, either at the reported location or at the registered address.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Vehicles assessed to be illegally modified will have to be inspected at authorised inspection centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: When TP officers on patrol detect a speeding vehicle with suspected illegal modifications, the case will be referred to LTA for further investigation.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: My residents complain a lot about vehicle noise, especially along Woodlands Ave 10.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: At night, it is usually very quiet and there will be occasional vehicles that are very, very loud.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: My question to the Senior Minister of State is whether we can use technology such as noise-detection cameras like those deployed in the UK and New York last year as stated in reports, to detect such vehicles.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is very hard – by the time they report, the vehicles are gone; unless the Police can be there all the time, and especially in the middle of the night.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As the Member has rightly pointed out, vehicle noise, particularly in the middle of the night, may even seem louder than what it would be, because of the low ambient surrounding noise.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Vehicle noise may not just be because of illegal modifications or speeding.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It could be the vehicle design, the way the driver drives a car and maintenance and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, we note the concerns of residents and we do work with TP as well as the National Environment Agency (NEA) to carry out enforcement operations when there is a need.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, currently, my understanding is that we have no plans to install such noise measuring instruments to detect violations, simply because it is actually quite challenging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But at the moment, there are currently no plans.
